methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates multiple complementary modalities (bulk WGS at 100x with a well-described NYGC pipeline using Mutect2/Strelka2/Lancet, scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, flow cytometry, Western, confocal, cytotoxicity assays, and AlphaFold2-Multimer structural modeling) which strengthens causal inference about antigenic escape. Important acknowledged limitations include no formal sample size calculation (n=21), two cases (MM-62, MM-63) using NA12878 as a mismatched germline control with only partial mitigation (PoN + gnomAD filtering), and primary patient-cell experiments performed only once due to material scarcity. Cell-line experiments are in biological triplicate with appropriate two-way ANOVA + Tukey multiplicity correction and four-parameter logistic IC50 fitting with profile-likelihood 95% CIs. Statistical reporting is strong for in vitro work (effect sizes, exact p values in Supplementary Tables 5-8), though inferential statistics on the clinical cohort are limited to a Kaplan-Meier PFS estimate without multivariable modeling or comparison between escape and non-escape subgroups.
methodological_rigor.statistical_justification: Appropriate tests used, multiplicity corrected, CIs reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The clinical component is a multi-institutional retrospective case series of 21 relapsed/refractory MM patients post-talquetamab with correlative preclinical functional validation, mapping to Oxford LoE 4 (small, non-randomized, no formal comparator cohort). Clinical/translational relevance is high: findings directly inform mechanisms of resistance to an FDA-approved GPRC5D TCE, demonstrate that antibody-based screening may miss epitope mutations with retained surface expression (p.Asp239Asn), and provide mechanistic rationale for bivalent/biparatopic TCE designs (forimtamig retained activity against several talquetamab-resistant mutants). The work has immediate implications for clinical dosing strategy, patient selection assays (genomic rather than flow-based), and next-generation TCE/CAR-T design including dual-antigen targeting.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the most applicable standard given the observational case-series design with correlative molecular work (ARRIVE n/a, no RCT so not CONSORT, not a biomarker-prognostic study per REMARK). Methods are detailed and transparent: ethics approvals from five institutions, trial identifiers (NCT04108195, NCT04634552), inclusion criteria, IMWG response definitions, extensive supplementary tables for patient characteristics (Supp Table 1), reagents (Supp Table 10), and p-values (Supp Tables 5-8). Patient flow and the swimmer/KM plots describe cohort composition clearly. Data availability text appears partially redacted but references deposition of prior scATAC/scRNA data in GEO (GSE199373, GSE199268, GSE199359); current WGS/scRNA deposition and code links are redacted in the blinded manuscript, so the reproducibility posture cannot be fully verified.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper substantially extends prior work (Lee et al. Nat Med 2023 [ref 13], Derrien et al. Nat Cancer 2023 [ref 20], Ma et al. Blood 2025 [ref 16]) that already reported biallelic GPRC5D deletions, some SNVs, and epigenetic silencing in smaller cohorts (n=2-8). The novel contributions are (i) a markedly larger multi-institutional post-TCE cohort (n=21) with systematic classification of three mutational patterns, (ii) functional demonstration that most GPRC5D SNVs cluster in GPCR-conserved ER-to-membrane trafficking motifs causing ER trapping, (iii) differential sensitivity profiling of monovalent (talquetamab) vs bivalent (forimtamig) TCEs against epitope mutants with structural modeling, and (iv) mechanistic linkage of epigenetic GPRC5D silencing to t(11;14) B-cell-like chromatin state. This is a meaningful conceptual and empirical extension rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical flow from clinical cohort description through genomic classification, functional validation, structural rationale, and epigenetic mechanism. The abstract is quantitatively grounded (68.4% escape rate, three mechanisms) and accurately reflects the paper. Figure captions are detailed and standalone-interpretable, with explicit statistical annotations and E:T ratios. Minor issues: some figure legends are duplicated verbatim in the text, a typo in Fig. 6d legend ('n = for each cell line'), and sentences in the Results occasionally pack many sub-events (e.g., the MM-61 nine-subclone list) that would benefit from a summary table in the main text.

key_strengths: Largest post-talquetamab resistance cohort to date (n=21) with integrated WGS/scRNA/scATAC profiling
Systematic mechanistic classification of three antigenic escape patterns with functional validation in K562 and JJN3 cell lines
Demonstrates clinically important dissociation between flow-based GPRC5D detection and TCE sensitivity (e.g., p.Asp239Asn, p.Tyr257Ser), with direct implications for patient selection assays
Comparative dose-response data for monovalent (talquetamab) vs bivalent (forimtamig) TCEs supports biparatopic design strategies
Structural rationale via cryo-EM template (PDB 9IMA) and AlphaFold2-Multimer modeling corroborates functional findings
Clear translational framing including caution against sub-therapeutic TCE dosing and genomic screening recommendations
key_concerns: Primary patient-cell experiments performed only once due to material limitations (acknowledged but limits replication confidence)
Two WGS cases used NA12878 as mismatched germline control, which may leave residual germline-contamination risk despite PoN/gnomAD filtering
No formal statistical comparison between escape and non-escape subgroups on clinical covariates, and small subgroup sizes preclude multivariable modeling
Epigenetic silencing mechanism rests on a single patient (MM-10), making the t(11;14)-linked claim correlative rather than causal
Data and code availability statements are redacted in the blinded text, so reproducibility posture for new sequencing data cannot be independently verified
Minor caption typos and some redundancy between figure legends and body text
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorous, multimodal mechanistic study expanding the understanding of GPRC5D antigen escape with clear clinical implications for a currently used TCE class; scope, novelty increment over refs 13/16/20, and translational actionability justify a tier-1 oncology venue with minor revisions.
